# Starlapse

> Long-exposure night sky camera for iPhone. An iPhone frame caps at about one second, so Starlapse stacks hundreds of one-second frames, aligned on the stars, into one long exposure. Free on the App Store; Starlapse Pro (one-time $4.99) adds meteor shower events and where to aim for them.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6801191027
- Source code (MIT): https://github.com/fortunto2/starlapse
- Privacy policy: https://starlapse.app/privacy/

## What it does

- Manual camera that stays locked: ISO, shutter, focus, white balance, lens
- Stacking from 10 seconds to an hour of collected light; pinpoint stars (aligned on the stars), star trails, clean landscape
- Night time-lapse where every frame is its own stack
- Meteor detector: keeps clips of anything that crosses the sky, places each meteor on the sky and names its shower
- Aiming overlay: planets, bright stars, the Moon, the Milky Way; where to point for tonight's meteor shower (40° off the radiant, clear of the Moon), for the user's location
- Shower alerts: a local notification on the evening of each good meteor night from the user's location
- Sky meter (1.1): sky brightness in magnitudes per square arcsecond, Bortle class and naked-eye limiting magnitude, computed from the catalogue stars (Yale Bright Star Catalogue) in each stack
- Optional sky dataset: readings and photos contributed for light-pollution research, location rounded to about 10 km, deletable from the app

## Honest limits

- iPhone aperture is fixed; the app shows what each lens gives up
- A single frame is about one second; everything longer is stacked
- iOS stops the camera in the background; the app keeps the screen on and dims it
- A tripod is required

## Languages

App: English, Hindi, Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, French, Arabic, German, Italian, Turkish, Spanish.
